items.reasons: Neither return says anything that the installed client, the repository or the sources contradict. /mcp and /context are commands the user runs and the model cannot invoke (C1, C2, C3). ToolSearch loads deferred tools (T2). /plugin is a real interactive command (R8, R10, R43), so its absence from the headless command list (C4) is a weakness in B, not a false statement. The current line is contradicted: CLAUDE.md:3 tells the model to inspect with /mcp and /context, and C1 and C2 show it cannot invoke either, so 'neither' loses. The executed comparison ties A and B on every preregistered measure (correct, answered and no_builtin_skill, 9 of 9 each). It also ties them on the descriptive loading and execution counts (loaded_schema 9, executed_target 6 each). By design every question could be settled from the tool list, and unsettleable claims are listed as not tested, so the fallback was never exercised. That fallback is the one place where the texts diverge, and it decides the choice. CLAUDE.md loads in every non-fork subagent (harness-rules-cleanup.md:39) and in unattended claude -p runs, where no approver answers (harness-rules-convergence-20260922.md:194). In those runs B's 'ask for the relevant /plugin, /mcp or /context output' asks for output that no model in the chain can produce (C1, C2). That includes /plugin, which the headless command list lacks (C4), so the run ends on a question no one can answer. A's 'report it as unconfirmed and name the command that would' gives a truthful final status in headless runs. In interactive sessions it still tells the user which command to run. It does not forbid asking, so it stays compatible with the client's own pattern of asking the user (C1, C2, R15) and with R59's point that someone is there to answer in human-in-the-loop sessions. It also matches R63 (say exactly what you left out and why) and, as support only, the stop rule in AGENTS.md:15. On paper B covers more. T1 lists agents among plugin components, and both R27 and the repository's handbook (token-session-handbook.md:67) separate listed tools from a successful call. But A produced the same measured loading and execution as B, so B's extra sentences bought no observed change. For an agents-only plugin, A's gap leads to an 'unconfirmed' report rather than a claim. B's 'available read-only diagnostics' also opens a path to evidence from settings or separate CLI connections, which does not show what the running session loaded (R44, R20, NF3). No run took that path (cli_diagnostic was 0 in every arm). A is three lines against B's six, and the file loads into every session and every non-fork child. With equal measured behavior, the shorter text is preferable. Cost and duration are not compared, as the input directs. Interactive sessions, other models and unsettleable claims remain untested, and round 1 split evenly, so confidence is moderate.
